extra_quotes: We implement channel waveguides that restrict incident 41-nm-wavelength light to a few modes with defined spatial profiles and propagation constants.

Following the design (d = 0.14 μm, Λ = 0.19 μm, h = 0.26 μm), we fabricated a 100 μm × 100 μm-large device via electron -beam lithography and inductively coupled plasma reactive ion etching of a 0.5 -μm-thick crystalline silicon membrane

To investigate the polarization analyzer, we generated an EUV attosecond pulse train via high-harmonic generation by focusing a near-infrared laser pulse (central vacuum wavelength 1.035 μm, pulse duration <190 fs, pulse energy 1 mJ) into an argon gas target.

The realized polarization contrast amounts to ~64 % of the numerical prediction despite the etched channels’ roughness, uncertainties in the achieved etch depth (see Fig. S4), a possible oxidation of the analyzer surface, uncertainties in silicon’s refractive index, and a possible ellipticity of the incident polarization states
